decision_differences.audited_prompt: someoneにsomethingをさせる（相手に直接働きかけ、強制する場合も）
まして〜はなおさら（否定的な内容を受け、より難しい例を加えることが多い）

decision_differences.resolution: The prior group KEEP was independently confirmed; Oxford explicitly treats rob somebody of something as a synonym of deprive for the figurative deprivation sense.

decision_differences.audited_prompt: somethingを言おうとする（くだけた表現で、言いたいことを間接的に示す）
somethingについて責任がある（特に悪い結果の原因として責められる含み）
decision_differences.resolution: The prior group KEEP remains compatible: both existing alternatives fit when the object is a bad result; the single-entry prompt adds the bad-result blame nuance.

decision_differences.audited_prompt: 考え直してみると（先の判断を変えるときに使う）
decision_differences.resolution: Cambridge defines the phrase as used to change a decision already made; this pragmatic function is not explicit in the current Japanese gloss.

decision_differences.audited_prompt: someoneをきつく叱る（くだけた表現）
decision_differences.resolution: Oxford marks tell somebody off informal. The current gloss captures intensity but not register; chew someone out also fits the informal qualified prompt.

decision_differences.audited_prompt: somethingをして罰を免れる（悪い行為について批判も受けずに済む）
decision_differences.resolution: The current gloss names punishment but leaves wrongdoing and escaping criticism implicit; Cambridge defines get away with as avoiding punishment or criticism for something wrong.
E0151 actually contains “as if he were somebody,” which does not match this canonical or its Japanese prompt. Isolated for upstream source/sense correction.

decision_differences.audited_prompt: someoneが自由に使える状態で（改まった表現）
decision_differences.resolution: Cambridge explicitly labels at someone’s disposal formal; the neutral, broader alternative does not preserve this register for the qualified prompt.
The Japanese gloss expresses logical coherence, while the sense key also includes understandability and E0158 may use that reading; isolated for upstream meaning/sense alignment.

decision_differences.draft_prompt: 要点を押さえた（簡潔で、余計な情報を加えない）
decision_differences.audited_prompt: 要点を押さえた（簡潔で、余計な情報を加えない）
decision_differences.resolution: Oxford describes to the point as concise and without extra information; Cambridge defines on point as informal/perfect, which does not preserve that meaning.

decision_differences.draft_prompt: someoneに腹を立てる（くだけた表現で、mad atは主に米語）
decision_differences.audited_prompt: someoneに腹を立てる（くだけた表現で、mad atは主に米語）
decision_differences.resolution: Cambridge labels the angry sense informal and mad at mainly US; the neutral alternative loses the qualified register/region.

decision_differences.draft_prompt: ダイエットを始める（継続中の状態ではなく開始を指す）
decision_differences.audited_prompt: ダイエットを始める（継続中の状態ではなく開始を指す）
decision_differences.resolution: The card says go on a diet, an onset; be on a diet is an ongoing state and diet does not encode starting. Added the natural onset paraphrase start dieting.

decision_differences.draft_prompt: そのうえ（話し言葉で強調して情報を付け足す）
decision_differences.audited_prompt: そのうえ（意外な点・より重要な点を付け加えて強調する）
decision_differences.resolution: Cambridge and Oxford support surprising/interesting or more-important added information, but do not establish a spoken-only restriction. Moreover retains the more-important sense; in addition does not reliably convey it.
